CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 9, 2018
 NEW BUSINESS

C.*  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE
  DEFAULT RATE TIER

  Recommendation: That the City Council select a default rate of 50% renewables (Clean
  Power) for all customers.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and provided
  a broad overview of the Clean Power Alliance program including the billing process and
  options for opting out of program.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested that a flyer explaining the program be sent with
  the first bill so customers are not confused. COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN concurred
  with the suggestion. Senior Planner Naughton noted that two flyers explaining the
  program will be mailed to all customers before the first bill arrives but she can check to
  see if that can be done.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN, Senior Planner Naughton noted that
  customers have the option of adjusting their rate tier either up or down, or opting out of
  the program at any time; and further reviewed the rate differences for the three rate tiers,
  noting that customers will see a slightly higher bill as compared to SCE with the 100%
  renewables option.

  Discussion ensued concerning the rates for the three default choices and the customers’
  options for opting out of the program or changing the rate tier.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reviewed the correspondence received from Michelle
  Leahy, City of Ojai, as revised, suggesting that the City select the default rate at 100%
  renewables; and concurred with many points raised in the letter. He suggested that, in
  order to have to have the greatest positive impact on the environment and reduce the
  City’s carbon footprint, the COUNCIL select the default rate tier of 100% renewables. He
  further suggested that in selecting the default rate tier of 100% renewables, the City also
  take steps to educate resident as to their options including how to opt out of the program
  or change their rate tier.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that although he agrees with the
  importance of environmental stewardship, he does not believe that selecting the highest
  default rate tier and forcing people to change their tier or opt out if they do not want that
  selection is in the best interest of the City’s constituents. He commented that people
  should be able to make their own choices.

  Discussion ensued concerning the default selection options.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that constituents will have a choice and be able
  to make changes if necessary for their individual circumstances.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 9, 2018
   MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she is supportive of selecting the default
  rate of 100% renewable given that residents will ultimately have a choice and it is the
  better option form an environmental stewardship perspective.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN
  explained the EAC’s rationale for recommending the default rate be set at 50%
  renewables, noting that given the information they had at the time of the meeting, they
  believed the 50% renewables option was best, in part because it had a neutral effect on
  residents’ bills. He further commented that he received additional information after that
  meeting, including at the CCA Board meeting and in Ms. Leahy’s letter that lead him to a
  different recommendation.

  Also in response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN
  noted that the City can change the default rate on an annual basis.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that she too is supportive of selecting the
  default rate of 100% renewable because it is good for the environment; and the City has
  the infrastructure and the ability to support it and residents have a choice.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL SELECT A DEFAULT RATE OF 100%
  RENEWABLES FOR ALL CUSTOMERS AND PROVIDE INFORMATION TO
  RESIDENTS INFORMING THEM OF THEIR OPTIONS WITH REGARD TO
  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Zerunyan

OLD BUSINESS

A.*  PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT OVERVIEW AND APPROVAL OF AMENDMENT OF
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TRIPEPI SMITH FOR SIX-MONTHS
  SERVICE OF CONTINUED PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT SUPPORT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: (1) receive and file the Public Engagement
  Update Report and (2) approve an amendment to the Professional Services Agreement
  with Tripepi Smith for monthly service in an amount not to exceed $4,294.58 per month
  for an additional six-month period beginning November 1, 2018.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he unfortunately has to excuse
  himself from the meeting, noting that in general, the presentation shows the value of the
  Contract Cities model and Tripepi Smith has met and exceeded his expectations.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 9, 2018
   John Barilone, Tripepi Smith reviewed the metrics and statistics associated with the City’s
  digital media platforms including Facebook, Instagram and Nextdoor, noting that there is
  an upward trend in the data.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that these efforts, supported by Tripepi Smith,
  have far exceed her expectation from the initial discussions regarding strategic marketing
  and the need to utilize analytics.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL expressed her appreciation for Tripepi Smith’s efforts in
  working toward the City’s social media and marketing objectives and noted that her hope
  is that ultimately, staff will continue gain the expertise necessary to continue these efforts,

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN echoed the previous comments and noted that these
  strategic efforts have not gone unnoticed.

  MAYOR HUFF commented that she too is appreciative of Tripepi Smith’s efforts in
  achieving the City’s marketing goals and objectives and in training staff, but it is her
  preference that staff carry on from here. She commented that she does not believe it
  necessary to maintain the same level of service for the next six months. She suggested
  extending for only three months or possibly cutting back on some of the services.

  Discussion ensued concerning the amount that has been spent thus far on the Tripepi
  Smith agreement and the projected amount for the next six months. Assistant City
  Manager Davis reviewed the contracts and the funds expended to date. Further
  discussion ensued concerning the positive impact these efforts have had on the City’s
  image in the community and in keeping the community informed.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ stressed the importance of having the ability to analyze
  the data and adjust messages to utilize strategic marketing noting that the COUNCIL
  needs to also consider the return on investment.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she is fully supportive of staff’s
  recommendation with the understanding that in that six months staff will be gaining the
  expertise to take over many of these duties and functions.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided an overview
  of the City’s efforts related to the use of Nextdoor specifically and the assistance Tripepi
  Smith has provided related to those efforts.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL (1) RECEIVE AND FILE THE PUBLIC
  ENGAGEMENT UPDATE REPORT; (2) APPROVE AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH TRIPEPI SMITH FOR
  MONTHLY SERVICE IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $4,294.58 PER MONTH
  FOR AN ADDITIONAL SIX-MONTH PERIOD BEGINNING NOVEMBER 1, 2018.

  AYES:  Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Huff
  ABSENT:  Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 9, 2018

A.  PROPOSED TREE REMOVAL – COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO

  COST OF APPROXIMATELY $2,500; AND (2) REFER REDESIGN OF THE
  COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO AREA TO THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION AFTER THE TREE HAS BEEN REMOVED.

B.  BUSINESS LICENSE TAX ADMINISTRATION SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Amendment No. 3 to the agreement

  administration services as outlined in the scope of services attached thereto, all to the

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per agenda

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL, Administrative Services Director

  the City will remain the same, with the only change being the addition of the business
  license tax administration services.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE AN AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY
  AND AVENU INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS/MUNISERVICES FOR BUSINESS
  LICENSE TAX ADMINISTRATION SERVICES AS OUTLINED IN THE SCOPE
  OF SERVICES PRESENTED, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
OCTOBER 9, 2018
 D.  RESOLUTION NO. 2431 ESTABLISHING PART-TIME OFFICE ASSISTANT JOB
  CLASSIFICATION, DESCRIPTION AND RESPECTIVE PAY RANGE WITHIN THE PART-
  TIME EMPLOYEE GROUP

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2431 establishing the
  classification, description and pay range for Office Assistant within the Part-Time

  ASSISTANT WITHIN THE PART-TIME EMPLOYEE GROUP.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan

MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she and MAYOR HUFF attended the
